transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I’ve taken on way too much lately—new projects, workshops, fixing up the studio, client calls. It all seemed manageable at first, but now the deadlines are piling up and I’m worried about the mortgage.
Around the time you started taking on all these projects, did you find that you needed much less sleep than usual while still feeling full of energy?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid close attention to my sleep—I just know I’ve been trying to keep up with everything.
During that time when you started all those projects, did you feel unusually high, elated, or on top of the world?
Most days, yes, I felt unusually buoyant—like everything with the studio and garden was finally falling into place. But I’d also snap at people if they questioned my plans or brought up the invoices.
Have you ever had a period in your life lasting at least two weeks where you felt deeply down, depressed, or lost interest in almost everything?
I’m not sure. I can’t think of a time when I felt that way for two weeks straight.
Have you ever experienced a period like this in the past where you felt unusually energized, buoyant, or took on lots of projects?
I honestly can’t think of another time like this. I’ve had busy stretches before, but nothing stands out as being unusually energized or taking on so many things at once.
Have these behaviors caused severe problems or disruption in your ability to work or manage your day-to-day life?
Yes. My illustration deadlines have slipped, and colleagues have had to check in on me. I also spent money I needed to keep the studio secure, and now the mortgage is at risk because I overcommitted.
